newsitem.title: USA: Lower Argentina soy crop due dry weather - attache.
newsitem.headline: Lower Argentina soy crop due dry weather - attache.

text.p: Dry weather during February and March and poor soil moisture conditions in key soybean producing provinces led Argentina to recently lower its soybean crop forecast, a U.S. agricultural attache said.

In a report dated April 23 released in Washington this week, the attache said the detrimental effect of the moisture deficit was increased by recent higher than normal temperatures, especially for the important growing regions of Cordoba and Santa Fe provinces.
Some damage due to frost had also been reported, the attache said.
On April 16, Argentina cut its 1996/97 soybean forecast to 12.86 million tonnes from 13.5 million tonnes seen prior.
"Reportedly, the reduction could have been more severe, but some recent rainfall proved beneficial to second crop beans," the attache wrote.
Argentina also shaved its forecast for the sunseed crop to 5.17 million tonnes from 5.4 million tonnes.

The attache said harvest results had demonstrated lighter weight seed in some areas and lower than expected yields, especially in areas where the crop was planted late. Reduced moisture availability also had a detrimental effect, he wrote.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.
In its April World Supply and Demand Report, USDA pegged the Argentina soybean crop at 13.25 million tonnes.
